subject: Lamp Health — Dedicated capacity activation & policy alignment
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria@lamphealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Li <evan.li@lamphealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity onboarding — kickoff

Sean,

Thanks for the intro earlier. Lamp Health is ready to kick off the dedicated GPU pool onboarding. High level: we want predictable latency for our inference endpoints and a clear autoscale / burst policy so we don't get bill shock during peak clinical workloads. Our target go-live for the pilot is April 15, and procurement expects to issue a PO by March 24.

To get started, could you confirm the recommended baseline pool size (GPU type + count), your autoscale/burst defaults, and any region recommendations? Also please include the SOW and any network preflight checklist we should share with our infra team.

I'll loop procurement on follow-ups. Attaching our latest capacity estimates (capacity_model_v3.csv).

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform
Lamp Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria@lamphealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity onboarding — kickoff

Maria — great to hear, and thanks for the capacity model. Looping in Monica (CS lead), Aditya (capacity engineering), and Kimberly (solutions) so we can align on a rapid, low-risk turn-up.

Proposed kickoff plan (short):
- Baseline pool: recommend 6 x A100-80GB (accelerator choice based on your token mix); we can start in us-east-1 or us-west-2 depending on your preference.
- Autoscale: target proactive scale at 60% GPU utilization, reactive scale across 3 steps to preserve latency.
- Burst policy: allow short (max 20m) burst to 2x baseline for traffic spikes; burst capacity billed as usage, with alerting thresholds.
- Network: VPC peering + dedicated service endpoints; we'll provide a network_preflight checklist.
- SOW & Ops: attaching SOW draft (SOW_LampHealth_v1.pdf) and network preflight. Please review procurement notes in the SOW — pricing on this draft reflects a 12-month reserved baseline with burst usage billed overage.

Kickoff meeting: proposed Mon Mar 6, 10:00 AM PT — 45m to finalize pool size, agree autoscale knobs, and lock the PO cutover window.

Owners & next steps:
- Sean: schedule kickoff and commercial approvals.
- Monica: run preliminary sizing review and validate runbook.
- Aditya: review capacity_model_v3.csv and confirm kernel/quantization guidance.
- Kimberly: prepare migration/runbook for prefix cache & KV cache warm-up.

If that sounds good I'll book the time.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Manager, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Maria Gomez <maria@lamphealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-03T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity onboarding — kickoff (technical notes)

Quick technical notes from CS/impl:
- Pool sizing: 6 x A100 is a reasonable starting point but recommend we validate with a 48h soak using real traffic (we can simulate with your capacity_model_v3.csv). If latency tail > 150ms at peak, add 2 GPUs.
- Autoscale triggers: prefer a hybrid metric: queue length (> 20 requests) + sustained GPU util > 65% for 90s to avoid flapping. Scale steps: +25%, +50%, +100% (cap at 2x baseline unless otherwise agreed).
- Burst behavior: allow ephemeral burst nodes in a separate ephemeral pool (non-reserved) to keep reserved baseline predictable. Ephemeral should be isolated to avoid preemption impact on baseline.
- Cost controls: enable token-level cost alerts and set soft throttle at 1.5x baseline spend to warn before hard limits.
- Optimization: recommend shipping a quantization profile to reduce memory; we can evaluate FP16 vs 4-bit for batch work.

I'll prepare a short runbook excerpt for the kickoff (warm-up steps, cache priming, and rollback).

—Monica
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

1) Region preference: we prefer us-east-1 for data residency and lower latency to our east-coast clinics. Is the A100 capacity available in us-east-1 for this timeframe? If not, we need a fallback region and a clear failover plan.

2) Procurement: PO on track for Mar 24. Procurement will need the final SOW and a breakdown of reserved vs burst charges by Mar 16 to complete approval.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity onboarding — kickoff (confirmation & next steps)

Thanks, everyone — quick alignment following internal capacity checks.

Decisions and immediate next steps (agreed):
- Baseline pool: provision 6 x A100-80GB in us-east-1 if capacity available by provisioning window; fallback to us-west-2 with automated routing rules if not. Aditya to confirm by Tue Mar 14.
- Autoscale: hybrid triggers (queue length + sustained GPU util > 65%); scale steps +25% / +50% / +100% with a hard cap at 2x baseline. Burst allowance: ephemeral pool up to 2x baseline for bursts up to 20 minutes.
- Billing: reserved baseline (monthly commit) + overage billing for ephemeral bursts; Sean will update SOW to include a per-minute burst rate and an illustrative monthly example for procurement. SOW update due Mar 16.
- Network: Lamp Health to run network_preflight.xlsx with their infra team. Kimberly will provide a step-by-step VPC peering checklist and a short runbook for warm-up and rollback.
- Kickoff meeting: confirmed Mon Mar 13, 10:00 AM PT (45m) — agenda to finalize region, lock SOW, and run through network checklist. Calendar invite to follow.

Action owners:
- Aditya Rao: confirm region capacity and provide fallback QoS plan (due 2028-03-14).
- Monica Patel: bring runbook excerpt and soak validation plan to kickoff.
- Kimberly Park: produce network checklist + peering runbook (due 2028-03-16).
- Sean Gallagher: update SOW with burst billing example and send final SOW to procurement (due 2028-03-16).

Attachments referenced: SOW_LampHealth_v1.pdf, network_preflight.xlsx, capacity_model_v3.csv.

I'll book the Mar 13 slot and circulate the updated SOW link.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
